newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: New S.Lanka court to try terrorism law detainees.
newsitem.headline: New S.Lanka court to try terrorism law detainees.

text.p: Sri Lanka will set up a new high court to try people charged under the country's terrorism law, a senior government minister told Reuters on Thursday.
Justice and Constitutional Affairs Minister Gamini Peiris said the new court was needed to dispose of cases quickly under the Prevention of Terrorism Act.
Figures from the Attorney-General's office show that 966 people have been indicted under the Act since 1994.

Sri Lanka applies the Act to people suspected of being involved in terrorist activities, including helping Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, who are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in the island's north and east.
The LTTE are fighting a 13-year-old war against the Sri Lankan army and the government has accused them of killing hundreds of people during attacks on civilian targets.
The government also exercises emergency regulations to arrest people suspected of consipiring against the state. The Attorney-General's office says 438 people were being tried under these laws.
